items.title: High-security prisoner used soap to escape despite being handcuffed and chained to officer

Personnel at RAF Lakenheath were told to take cover on 13 November after “suspected unauthorised drone activity”. The US air force confirmed the so-called Charlie alert at the time, the second-highest threat level, but released few details. Sirens could be heard at the base . Iran is suspected of being involved. The Department for Work and Pensions took down several systems that appeared to still be offline on Saturday morning. David Knott, who led government technology until December 2025, said much infrastructure was outdated, and underinvestment in defence and increasing sophistication of attacks meant it was only getting more vulnerable. items.title: Unpaid TV licence or cycling on pavement could bar people from settling in UK
items.desc: Exclusive: New immigration rules will introduce strict threshold where any adult conviction triggers mandatory refusal People could be barred from settling in the UK over minor infractions such as cycling on the pavement or failing to pay a TV licence, ministers have been warned before the introduction of new “earned settlement” rules. Under the plans, which are to come into effect next year, securing indefinite leave to remain will become significantly harder for many people. The rules introduce a strict new threshold where any adult conviction resulting in a court disposal – including fines, community orders, conditional cautions, and absolute or conditional discharges – triggers mandatory refusal. This week, Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta launched its Muse AI assistant in the UK and is encouraging users to let it shop and make restaurant reservations. The bot is given access to the user’s email if they give it permission, and it can make restaurant bookings and go shopping on the user’s behalf. Continue reading...

items.title: The Com: the global cybercrime network posing a ‘chilling threat’ to children
items.desc: FBI estimates thousands of people identify as members, or recent members, of group linked to indecent images of girls and blackmail It sounds benign: the Com, short for the Community. But crime agencies around the world warn that it is far from that and the young cybercriminals involved are causing havoc and putting children at chilling, sickening risk. Beau-Jack Mensforth was jailed by a UK judge on Friday for his activities as part of the Com. He was one individual operating from his bedroom in north-east England, but there are probably thousands more like him and parents are being urged by police to be aware and to check their children’s devices. Continue reading...

items.desc: Timothy X Atack wrote Tiny Alarms after workshops with children, who felt theirs would be the last generation of humans Tiny, a 12-year-old schoolgirl, is an ecojustice influencer, whose funny and disconcerting takes on the climate crisis go viral. She is also an alien, sent to warn humankind of its impending doom – but her mission is far more difficult than she anticipated. This is the plot of Tiny Alarms, the first winner of Shakespeare’s Globe’s new climate playwriting prize. It was inspired by the real beliefs of schoolchildren for whom its author, Timothy X Atack, ran creative writing workshops exploring ideas around the far future. Continue reading...

items.title: UK’s taste for cow’s milk sours as sales hit record low
items.desc: Environmental and animal welfare concerns, and taste preferences, are behind rising popularity of vegan alternatives Has milk gotta lotta bottle? It may not have as much as it used to, with official data showing Britons are buying less cow’s milk than at any point since records began. Guardian analysis of the government’s family food survey shows the average person bought 1.8 pints (1,024ml) of cow’s milk a week in 2024-25 – the lowest level in the record’s 52-year history and less than half the amount of milk bought in 1974.
